snippet.text: `Lowering` holds one proposal against the fence, and `refusal()` says why it fails. It refuses a decision-model executor, a refuted verdict, a `melian/injection-attempt` claim, and a defect a deterministic check co-reported. It refuses a P0, a target of `nit`, and any move but one step down. It refuses a target the table in force resolves `silent`, a table Melian could not read, and a proposal with no evidence at the head. `VerificationRecord.refusal(report)` says why a later report of a claim cannot follow the stored one: it is taken only when none is stored, when it is the stored report again, as a replay sends it, or when its verdict is stronger, and it then replaces the stored report whole. Otherwise the first report stands, its reason and lowering included, as [the decision](../decisions/2026-11-28-a-claims-first-report-stands.md) sets out.

The findings document is version 12, which adds `checkRuns`, the stamps above, each a check task and a request key, and lets a dismissal's `dismissedSighting` keep its check's stamp as `run`; version 11 reads unchanged. Version 11 lets a dismissal record `dismissedSeverity`, the severity the verdict showed each report at, which `recordDismissal` passes to `dismissFinding`. Beside it the dismissal records `dismissedSighting`, the finding as that revision showed it. The document also keeps per revision `inherited`, the restatement links of [issue #315](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/315). Version 10 reads unchanged; `test/fixtures/stored-v10/` holds a SQLite store main wrote at `d4e8d8df`, which its reopen test opens. Step 29 permits each merged member claim to retain its reported severity. Versions 8 and 9 read unchanged. `test/fixtures/stored-v9/` was recorded by main at `748dfe37`; its SQLite reopen test retains accepted triggers, affected proof and verification through a version-10 write. Version 9 adds optional `dismissedTrigger` to the lifecycle, with the accepted hash and affected proof hashes. Its migration branches on the source version: version 8 reads unchanged, with no invented accepted trigger; earlier versions keep their existing evidence upgrades. `test/fixtures/stored-v8/` was recorded by main at `e0a9d00f`. Its SQLite reopen test preserves the legacy older-revision behaviour, then records a new dismissal and proves its content binding survives another reopen. Version 7 added optional maps that hold verdicts by revision, producer and verifier version beside each sighting. Reports run sequentially. Within one verification task, confirmed outranks plausible, which outranks refuted for the same claim. `upsertVerification` asks core's `VerificationRecord.refusal` inside the report's commit, and `report_verdict` refuses a later report of a claim unless its verdict is stronger, so the first report keeps its reason and lowering and the refused call writes nothing. A replay of  [cut at 2 KiB]

- The verifier sees each root on a trusted line, `Dismissed d1 finding <id>`, and its failure scenario and evidence inside the findings boundary, never its reason. `report_verdict` takes `matches`, same or different by root ID. Its tool refuses a report that leaves out a listed root or names another, since Pi hands `prepareArguments` no conversation, and stores the answers on the record. A claim's first report keeps its answers, as it keeps its reason: a later report at an equal or weaker verdict is refused, and only a stronger verdict replaces them, with the rest of the record.

The goldens of conflicting reports change with it. Both orders now pair a lowered confirmed report with an unlowered plausible one, which leave the claim lowered either way: the weaker is refused after the stronger, and the stronger replaces the weaker before it. A replay after each report shows a replayed report taken and an equal plain report refused. The lowering refused for want of evidence is reported again without the lowering, and the lens's severity stands.

explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md, Writing rules: "Prefer short words and short sentences. If a sentence runs past about 25 words, find the seam." The sentence is nearly twice that length. It also passes the 45-word run that the root `overlong-sentence` guardrail flags in `docs/`. This is the longest of four sentences the change wrote past about 25 words. The other three are docs/guidelines/pipeline.md:528 (about 37 words, from "`upsertVerification` asks core's..."), docs/guidelines/pipeline.md:535 (about 37 words, "A claim's first report keeps its answers...") and the decision file's line 15 (about 35 words, "Both orders now pair...").

properties.failureScenario: A reader of core.md's verification section gets a 48-word sentence. It holds three acceptance conditions and the replacement rule, joined by a colon and commas. The guideline is meant to be readable at a glance, and here the reader has to parse it twice to see which clause the final "and it then replaces the stored report whole" belongs to. The root `overlong-sentence` guardrail (45 or more words in `docs/`) also flags the line when it is changed, at P3 advisory.
